cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a tukutuku panel, a traditional Māori woven lattice-work wall panel used to decorate meeting houses (wharenui), made from flax and reeds with characteristic geometric patterns — a well-documented Māori craft and architectural element.

physical.title: wall panel
physical.summary: Composite wall panel (tukutuku) for meeting house: peg-board base with horizontal wood slats (all painted dark red) and vertical reeds (stems of toetoe - Cortaderia spp.) on back, with cross-stitched design in natural and dyed New Zealand flax (Phormium tenax) strips on front, attached to reeds at back through holes in peg-board; design field divided into eight rectangular sections arranged in four vertical pairs, each section different (triangles, multiple diamonds, groups of triple lines, zigzag, multiple rectangles, large diamond, "V"s, multiple broad vertical lines) and each framed in yellow.
